claude-01c729d4.title: The summary card, and page titles
claude-01c729d4.note: Density removed from Queue, repeated page headings replaced with sr-only names and per-route document titles, and the Reviewed section deleted once it could not justify itself. Ends with the milestone declared complete.

claude-0cb7956e.title: The README says what shipped
claude-0cb7956e.note: Bringing the README and its architecture diagram back in line with the built product.

claude-31bb4686.title: Scoring the summaries
claude-31bb4686.note: The first session that judged the product's actual output. Real summaries were pasted in and scored, the owner diagnosed the takeaway cap as duration-blind before the code did, sections were resized, and a harness was specced by first asking what exactly it would verify. It ends with the attribution work discarded — the results were good enough without it.

claude-3426388e.title: Documenting the prompts
claude-3426388e.note: This export: deciding what a record of the work should be, and building it. The session is included because leaving it out would make the record incomplete on its first day.

claude-377a708a.title: Code review feedback, one item at a time
claude-377a708a.note: Four rounds of the same loop: paste a review finding, ask for an explanation and whether it is worth addressing, implement it into the working tree, look at it, then commit. The empty-string validation ruling came out of this.

claude-3816b4ef.title: Fifteen items of UI feedback
claude-3816b4ef.note: The longest UI session: each item explained as if to a novice user, options weighed, then applied. Read and Unread were removed entirely rather than restyled, reading-time estimates dropped for being visibly untrustworthy, and several decisions were reversed mid-session once seen on screen. Screenshots drive most of the second half.

claude-51e0b539.title: The PRD becomes canonical
claude-51e0b539.note: The split that governs every document since: PRD.md is the product specification and AGENTS.md keeps only engineering. Then two review findings, including the one that removed an optimisation because a missing row made the ledger harder to reason about than the row cost.

claude-53d8de9d.title: The UULF playlist prefix
claude-53d8de9d.note: The owner brought the finding — YouTube's feed can be filtered by swapping the channel prefix — and drove it to a decision: UULF only, so Shorts and live VODs never crowd the fifteen-entry feed.

claude-56317bcc.title: Which skills are installed
claude-56317bcc.note: A single question, kept for completeness.

claude-6175d3e7.title: A design milestone, and choosing daisyUI
claude-6175d3e7.note: A progress report that turned into inserting a whole UI/UX milestone before M4. shadcn was evaluated and daisyUI chosen, with the conflicting rules removed rather than left to contradict it.

claude-68c1db28.title: The chat cited the wrong episode
claude-68c1db28.note: A live defect — a true-crime question citing a Steve Jobs episode — traced to the fact that a cosine score cannot carry a relevance floor at any value, and fixed with a cross-encoder reranker. That exposed a second fault: superseded vector generations were never deleted above 100 chunks, because the delete batch size had been carried over from the upsert ceiling and never measured.

claude-6b0a45e9.title: The design phase, designed
claude-6b0a45e9.note: Wireframes argued over rather than accepted: the digest window dropped in favour of day groups, a calendar proposed for thirty channels, opening and finishing pulled apart. Six numbered critiques came back at the artifact. It produced docs/design.md and wired AGENTS.md to it the way it already pointed at the PRD.

claude-7163b283.title: The design phase, built
claude-7163b283.note: Nine steps, mostly 'proceed with step N'. The vocabulary ruling landed here — episodeId everywhere, videoId only at the feed boundary — and the session ended in a live error hunt over a newly added channel.

claude-8dd9ca45.title: What a channel actually is
claude-8dd9ca45.note: A product session first — explain the current model, diagram it, evaluate the owner's own proposal — and an implementation session second. Soft delete became a declined state, the schema was rewritten rather than migrated because nothing was deployed, and the back half is eight review findings worked one at a time, against some resistance to being handed all of them at once.

claude-90edcfdc.title: The Registry Durable Object
claude-90edcfdc.note: The first implementation session. The Registry DO, the identity middleware, and GET /me, then the User DO — with a detour into how to clear every migration and reapply it, which became the habit that eventually turned into the clean-local skill.

claude-96072d04.title: The cursor on clickable things
claude-96072d04.note: A small session with a general ruling inside it: use daisyUI rather than overriding it, written into the design guide before the controls were reclassified.

claude-9be0a26d.title: A false start
claude-9be0a26d.note: The same instruction as the next session, mistyped and abandoned a minute later. Kept because it happened.

claude-c6833921.title: Checking a new channel ingested
claude-c6833921.note: One prompt, asking whether a newly added channel's workers and summaries had run.

claude-cb72d979.title: Is M5 all that is left

claude-d4ad1ab7.title: The read experience, specced and built
claude-d4ad1ab7.note: The first feature worked end to end: spec, decisions taken one at a time, a two-phase plan, then implementation. Two rulings here outlived the session — that channel ids are asked for rather than resolved from @handles, and that the API is modelled on entities rather than roles, which killed OwnerRequest and every /owner/* route. It also contains the first transcript spike, whose finding was set aside for later.

claude-d82bad18.title: M3 split into seven chunks
claude-d82bad18.note: M3 was too big to hold, so it was broken into seven spec-and-plan pairs and the first chunks were built. A staging environment was stood up so the dev vector index was not the only one. The last few prompts are the first real summary coming back raw, and the owner rewriting the map prompt by hand.

claude-d91282ac.title: The API reference, specified and implemented
claude-d91282ac.note: Resumed from an earlier session, so it carries the whole arc. The rulings are the interesting part: the API enforces no authorization at all and the web is the only gate; the owner-specific channel route is removed; migrations stop being additive-only; and the plan is restructured to depend on nothing in M3. It ends by finding channel state in two places and specifying follows onto a single owner.

claude-e5fed134.title: The long-form feed, implemented
claude-e5fed134.note: Two prompts: walk me through the plan as if I were junior, then build it.

claude-e79bc0f7.title: A skill for wiping local Durable Object state
claude-e79bc0f7.note: Editing an applied migration means the local DO state has to go. This turned that chore into a skill, and settled two things that stuck: skills follow the open Agent Skills standard rather than a Claude-only format, and Node is pinned to the 22.x line rather than an exact patch.

claude-eb35f7e4.title: Chats, from PRD to walkthrough
claude-eb35f7e4.note: The largest session in the project: the chat feature specified, planned, built across five steps, then tested end to end through the API before the UI existed. Scope handling was argued down to component state with nothing in the URL, dedupe was removed in favour of grouping in the UI, and the last stretch is a visual walkthrough. It closes by auditing M4, M5 and M6.

claude-eda6b43d.title: A browser test client, then the transcript spike
claude-eda6b43d.note: Began as a way to read the API from a browser and became the session that settled how transcripts are fetched at all. Every Cloudflare egress path to YouTube failed from a DO-free spike Worker; a Bright Data unlocker was raised and dropped; DownSub was probed against its own API docs and a HAR capture, and chosen. The InnerTube fetcher was removed and its history rewritten. It closed on embeddings, dimensions, and the cron cadence.

claude-f1f6bf74.title: clean-local reaches the vector index
claude-f1f6bf74.note: Extending the skill to clear dev Vectorize, and pushing back on a name until the scope was right. It also added the skills install and remove commands, after the CLI's unscoped remove was found to delete the source.

claude-f6c585fa.title: The M3 ingestion spec, argued out
claude-f6c585fa.note: The longest design session in the project and almost no code. Dozens of review findings taken one by one, most of them answered with a question rather than an acceptance — lifecycle versions dropped, stale-run claims challenged on product grounds, ER diagrams and status tables requested to check the model held together. It ends with the decision to throw the schema away and start it over.

claude-f98fcb94.title: Naming it Said on Air
claude-f98fcb94.note: Three prompts: suggest names, find one with a free domain, write it into the PRD.
